before:
The airport for Puerto Vallarta, inside the urban area and just 1 km north of Marina Vallarta, which makes for very short transfers. It is also the gateway to Riviera Nayarit and the Jalisco coast, and works all year round.

It is growing fast. It served 6,803,500 passengers in 2024 and 6,947,700 in 2025, making it seventh busiest in Mexico overall and fifth busiest for international traffic, with 24 airlines flying to 57 destinations, 41 of them international.

For a British client the useful detail is that it takes direct flights from the United Kingdom as well as the United States and Canada.

The single runway is 3,100 metres at an elevation of just 7 metres. The two-storey terminal puts check-in and arrivals with customs and baggage on the ground floor.

It is officially Licenciado Gustavo Díaz Ordaz International Airport, after the former president, though nobody calls it that.
after:
The airport for Puerto Vallarta and Riviera Nayarit, 7.5 km north of the city centre, which makes for short transfers.

It handled 6,947,700 passengers in 2025, up from 6,803,500 in 2024, and the airport says 17 airlines fly here in 2026 on 54 routes. Traffic has since fallen: GAP, which runs it, counts 12.4 per cent fewer passengers from January to August 2026, after unrest in Jalisco in February led airlines to cancel flights.

There are no direct flights from Britain on record: the UK Civil Aviation Authority counted no passengers between the two in 2025, after 8,882 on charter flights from Manchester in 2024.

The single runway is 3,100 metres, at an elevation of just 7 metres.

Its full name is Licenciado Gustavo Díaz Ordaz International Airport, after the former president, though it is usually called Puerto Vallarta International Airport.

claims.note: On 22 February 2026 the army killed the leader of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel, which set off roadblocks and burning vehicles across the state (KATU, citing AP). GAP says the events affected travel demand, and Puerto Vallarta's traffic fell from March.

claims.claim: no direct flights from Britain on record, per the UK Civil Aviation Authority
claims.inAfter: There are no direct flights from Britain on record: the UK Civil Aviation Authority counted no passengers between the two in 2025, after 8,882 on charter flights from Manchester in 2024.
claims.note: Replaces 'it takes direct flights from the United Kingdom', which Wikipedia still says ('offering flights to and from Mexico, the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom'). The CAA's 2025 table of international routes from UK reporting airports (run 25 February 2026) has a single Puerto Vallarta row, Manchester: 0 passengers in 2025, 8,882 in 2024, all on charter flights. No other UK airport has a Puerto Vallarta row. TUI's own site refused automated reads (Akamai 403 to both tools), so no airline's plans for later seasons could be checked; the text therefore says 'on record' and names the year. The US and Canada are covered by the airport's own route and airline counts.

claims.claim: seventh busiest in Mexico, fifth for international traffic
claims.wasBefore: making it seventh busiest in Mexico overall and fifth busiest for international traffic
claims.why: Wikipedia contradicts itself (its text says seventh for 2025, its infobox eighth) and the national tables (AFAC, on gob.mx) sit behind an Akamai challenge. The operators' 2025 figures cannot settle it: Puerto Vallarta's 6.95 million is close to Felipe Ángeles's, whose 2025 total was not read. For international traffic GAP counts Tijuana's CBX users as international (4.09 million), which would put Tijuana ahead of Puerto Vallarta's 3.82 million, so the order depends on the definition.
